newsitem.title: PERU: Hopes dim for quick progress in Peru hostage talks.
newsitem.headline: Hopes dim for quick progress in Peru hostage talks.

text.p: Hopes dimmed on Saturday for any immediate break in Peru's 53-day hostage crisis as President Alberto Fujimori left the country for an economic forum in London.

No new meetings were slated between mediators, the government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home. Fujimori's planned absence until Tuesday made major breakthroughs unlikely anytime soon.
Mediators met on Thursday with Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas to restart talks between the rebels and the government that were broken off on Dec. 28.
But no evidence has emerged since then that the two sides are any closer to resuming the negotiations.
Early on Saturday, Fujimori departed for London in a new bid to rally foreign support for his tough handling of the crisis and salvage the country's image.
He was expected to make a one-day stopover in New York before flying onto London, where he planned to speak at a Latin American forum and meet with Prime Minister John Major.
The hostages passed another uneventful night and after dawn on Saturday police began playing romantic folk music from huge speakers in front of the mansion.

The relative calm followed a carnival-like atmosphere the previous day, when Mexican mariachis serenaded two Peruvian officials inside who had birthdays, rebels sang revolutionary hymns and shouted slogans and police blasted "criolla" folk music from huge seakers.
Young girls served free lemonade to police and reporters and a group of women decked a road with flowers to call for a peaceful outcome to the standoff.
But a four-hour visit to the hostages by medics to check their heart conditions underscored the unseen hardships and tensions of seven weeks of captivity.
Some 15 MRTA guerrillas stormed the ambassador's compound during a lavish cocktail party on Dec. 17 and seized hundred of hostages. They have since released most of the captives.
The rebels are demanding the release of more than 400 comrades held in Peruvian jails in exchange for freeing the captives.
Fujimori, whose brother Pedro is among the hostages, has refused to even discuss the demand but has pledged to seek a peaceful solution to the crisis.
